Non-volatile memory (NVM) enables the construction of in-memory database and file system systems by preserving data persistently on disk-like storage. To ensure data consistency, these critical applications rely heavily on algorithm-driven knowledge, which has driven the development of diverse techniques ranging from basic non-blocking locks to advanced lock-free methods. Although the field has seen significant advancements, there remains a scarcity of resources that provide a comprehensive overview of these approaches, their underlying mechanisms, and their real-world application. This article addresses that gap by offering a thorough survey of how algorithm-based data consistency strategies are implemented in NVM file systems and databases. We begin with an introduction to data consistency models specific to NVM, followed by an examination of the data structures and algorithms used to maintain it. Furthermore, we analyze the various data protection strategies employed in modern NVM applications, detailing the specific algorithmic choices made in each context. Finally, we explore emerging research directions and outstanding unresolved challenges within the NVM data management domain.

Information networks, such as the World Wide Web, are intricate systems that have generated significant interest regarding their internal architecture and the content they host. While traditional statistical methods can uncover basic network properties, they often fail to address content nuances effectively. This paper introduces the Hierarchical Document Topic Model (HDTM), a novel technique for analyzing information networks by jointly exploring both their structural and semantic dimensions. HDTM operates on a dual representation: a structural document-topic hierarchy and a topic-specific content hierarchy. Structurally, the approach treats a document as a collection of sub-documents organized in a hierarchy, each adhering to its distinct topic distribution. Concurrently, the content hierarchy tracks hierarchical topic progressions within documents. Empirical evaluations on a collection of medical documents demonstrate that HDTM effectively reveals information structures often obscured by standard methods, successfully balancing the exploration of network content and architecture.

This study investigates three-dimensional systems featuring two bodies interacting with a third via a $1/r$ potential, with particular attention given to non-escaping trajectories and those exhibiting very long escape times. We found that the statistical properties of these three-body configurations align well with predictions from uncorrelated random theories. Additionally, we developed an uncorrelated random model to estimate the escape duration for three-body systems, demonstrating strong agreement with actual simulations. These discoveries suggest that a complex dynamical system can display statistical regularities equivalent to those in simpler, less dynamic systems.

This study examines the suppression of prompt $\psi(2\text{S})$ mesons in the ALICE experiment's $\sqrt{s_{\text{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV lead-lead collisions, analyzing both their yield and the momentum-dependent nuclear modification factor ($R_{\text{AA}}$) alongside the transverse momentum ($p_{\text{T}}$) spectrum. Measurements are taken for $p_{\text{T}}$ ranging from 0 to 30 GeV/$c$ and across various rapidity values within the interval $-3.5 < y < 3.5$. The results indicate that prompt $\psi(2\text{S})$ production is more suppressed than that of the J/$\psi$ ($R_{\text{AA}}$) in the low $p_{\text{T}}$ region ($0 < p_{\text{T}} < 10$ GeV/$c$), yet becomes comparable in the higher $p_{\text{T}}$ regime ($10 < p_{\text{T}} < 30$ GeV/$c$). Additionally, the study investigates the influence of particle species on these findings by analyzing the balance between prompt J/$\psi$ production and b-hadron yields in terms of $R_{\text{AA}}$ and $p_{\text{T}}$.

We establish a correspondence between equivalence relations defined on the natural numbers and certain metric spaces within the framework of continuous logic through an isomorphism that preserves structure. Specifically, the compact complete metric spaces usually studied in this logical setting are demonstrated to be equivalent to the quotient of a compact complete metric space by an equivalence relation on $\mathbb{N}$, where both the spaces and the relations are equipped with uniformly controlled moduli. We further investigate how these logical structures behave under first-order expansions, analyzing the associated equivalence relations and their properties in detail.

This paper introduces a novel approach to software configuration management that utilizes singular value decomposition (SVD) on versioned source code to condense multiple related versions into one unified version. By representing versions as matrices of tokenized tokens, the method uses SVD to identify and merge similar versions, thereby reducing redundancy. The primary advantage of this technique emerges when a version undergoes significant similarity to others; in such cases, the version matrix rank drops, allowing less related versions to be effectively pruned. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm the approach's efficacy, successfully merging multiple related version sequences into single, high-quality outcomes.

Deep sequential models have proven effective in numerous applications, yet their performance often degrades when processing long sequences due to constraints in existing recurrent architectures. Although attention mechanisms offer a solution for sequence processing, existing attention-based models still require sequential processing, leaving a sequence length limit that hinders further performance gains. This paper introduces BilsttAttention, a novel deep sequential architecture designed to mitigate this issue. By combining features from both Bi-LSTM and attention mechanisms, our approach processes sequences in parallel, allowing for theoretically unlimited lengths. Empirical results across three datasets for speech synthesis confirm that BilsttAttention surpasses current state-of-the-art models, which were previously based only on self-attention or convolutional attention.

We report on X-ray polarization measurements of the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A) obtained using the Imaging Polarimetry on X-ray Timing Arrays (IXPE) satellite. The detected polarization degree is 3.4% ± 0.6% (statistical) ± 1.0% (systematic), with an polarization angle of 111° ± 6° (statistical) ± 10° (systematic) relative to the source's north-south axis. Our analysis indicates that the source count spectrum remains consistent with previous findings, showing no significant deviations. Furthermore, our findings support a synchrotron origin for X-ray emission, with polarized magnetic fields oriented roughly east-west, aligning with magnetic field orientations in the plane of the sky derived from radio observations of the entire remnant. Additionally, we explore potential contributions from inverse Compton scattering and an absorbed blackbody component to the source's emission profile.

The classic distinct subset sums problem requires every subset of a given set to have a unique sum. This study examines a relaxed variation: for any subset of size at most $\ell$, where $\ell \le n$, the sums must be unique. The primary objective is to determine the minimum size of such a set within $\{1, \dots, q\}$ and establish the smallest integer value $q$ (the capacity) that allows the construction of $n$ numbers satisfying these conditions. The analysis demonstrates that when $\ell$ scales as $n^{\delta}$ with $\delta < 1$, the optimal capacity is $O(1/\delta)$, whereas if $\ell$ is linear with exponent $\delta = 1$, the capacity is $O(n)$.

This study examines the equation of state for cold quark stars, specifically focusing on the impact of a deconfinement phase transition on their properties. We analyze two scenarios: one where the transition occurs at a finite critical chemical number density, and another where it is modeled as a crossover at a finite critical density. Our findings indicate that for both scenarios, the maximum mass and radius of the star remain unchanged if the critical parameters are identical. However, we observe a significant difference in how the maximum mass behaves under varying transition types: when treated as a first-order phase transition, the maximum mass can increase with higher critical parameters, whereas for a crossover transition, it remains constant. These results offer valuable insights into the nature of the deconfinement transition within cold quark stars.

The non-local compass state exhibits high susceptibility to damping, rendering it an ideal candidate for estimating this parameter in metrological settings. However, our analysis reveals a trade-off: while increased susceptibility enhances sensitivity, a high number variance within the compass state simultaneously hampers estimability. We demonstrate that for damping values susceptible to a single measurement, optimal compass states must have their number variance kept below a specific critical threshold. Consequently, the balance between damping susceptibility and estimability serves to delineate the viable parameter space for effective damping estimation using these states.

We introduce a novel methodology for characterizing and discriminating the geometry of distinct liquid jets, including gaseous-liquid jets, by analyzing their characteristic optical diffraction patterns. This approach offers a simple, non-invasive, and highly sensitive means of differentiating between various jet structures, such as conical and cylindrical forms, as well as distinguishing jets generated from different gases or liquids. The theoretical framework relies on light diffraction at the meniscus, with predictions showing strong agreement between them and experimental observations.

This paper introduces a novel mathematical model for viral replication, focusing on the mechanics of DNA synthesis during bacterial infection by *Escherichia coli*. We propose that synthesis results from "viral rolling," a process where the virus's surface metabolism facilitates movement akin to a spool, thereby enabling DNA synthesis. We further suggest that this rolling motion is governed by a molecular ratchet mechanism, driven by the asymmetric reduction of affinity between the virus and the host under the influence of energy dissipation. We formulate this hypothesis using a continuous-time Markov chain, analyzing its long-term behavior via a deterministic fluid approximation and a simplified two-state approximation in the form of a ordinary differential equation system. We validate our model against experimental data, demonstrating that these predictions align well with observed realities.

This study investigates the environmental contexts of 100 spiral galaxy warps, utilizing data from the Galaxy Zoo Tilted Spiral Project. We analyzed the proximity of 100 nearest neighbors to the main body and each spiral arm, as well as the local galaxy density within 100 kpc. The research distinguishes between two warp categories: Type U (upside-down) and Type S (asymmetric). Our findings indicate that S-type warps occur in environments with higher density and are exposed to stronger tidal forces than U-type warps. While both types are more prevalent in cluster outskirts than in the core regions, U-type warps show a greater likelihood of forming in clusters compared to S-type. Furthermore, S-type warped galaxies exhibit a higher incidence of interactions with neighbors compared to non-warped spirals or U-type warped ones. In contrast, the projected tidal shear and galaxy density within 100 kpc show no significant correlation with warp amplitude for either type. These results suggest that strong tidal fields and physical interactions with nearby galaxies are key factors in the formation of S-type warps.

We report on the first-principles investigation of topological properties in Rb$_2$SrBi$_4$ and RbCsBi$_4$, which are isostructural to Ba$_3$RbBi$_6$ and Ba$_3$KBi$_6$. These materials are predicted to be non-trivial topological insulators characterized by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant of (1111)1. In Rb$_2$SrBi$_4$, the phase symmetry is broken by doping, which shifts the Fermi level into the conduction band, resulting in a metallic state. Conversely, RbCsBi$_4$ exhibits a trivial band gap that closes upon doping, with the final state depending on the specific concentration of dopants introduced.

Driven by optical experiments, we investigate the dynamics of Born effective charges in the context of polaron motion within insulators and metals. Our findings reveal a significant disparity between the two systems: in pristine (disorder-free) conductors, optical experiments detect only the intrinsic Born effective charges of the host material, as the polycar's contribution vanishes due to zero nonadiabatic Born effective charge. Conversely, in insulators where the moving charge acquires a substantial positive contribution from its nonadiabatic Born effective charge, the motion acts similarly to that of a heavy charge carrier. This insight offers a novel perspective on interpreting optical data concerning polaron activity specifically in insulating materials.

We introduce a novel approach to analyze the statistical characteristics of dissipation in three-dimensional fluctuating hydrodynamics, a framework that extends the concept of fluctuating hydrodynamics to this dimension. Our findings reveal that the dissipation rate in this system shares analogous statistical features with those observed in deterministic direct numerical simulations of the Navier-Stokes equation used to describe turbulence. Specifically, fluctuating hydrodynamics yields a significantly lower maximum dissipation rate compared to the turbulent case, a result traceable to the presence of the noise term within the dissipation integral. Furthermore, turbulence is demonstrated to elevate the dissipation rate beyond the levels set by fluctuating hydrodynamics by actively amplifying small-scale fluctuations.

We offer a theoretical framework for magnetoelectric coupling, illustrated through a thought experiment involving the Witten effect: a magnetized electrically neutral entity is predicted to host internal charges due to magnetization. By applying semiclassical equations of motion to charged excitations, we analyze this scenario and identify two distinct forms of magnetoelectric coupling. The first, a "polar" effect, stems from the variation of the vector potential of the electromagnetic field within the system's phase space, implying that the system's action includes a term representing the integral of electromagnetic field strength wedged with the $U(1)$ connection of the internal phase space. The second arises when Lorentz forces alter the worldsheet of the system's worldvolume, adding a boundary term to the action where the internal $U(1)$ gauge field interacts with the external electromagnetic field. We examine these phenomena within string theory and various solvable ultraviolet completions of effective field theory, including abelian and non-abelian black holes as well as D-branes.

We demonstrate that diffusion can be intensified within delayed nonlinearity systems, leading to an effective reduction in dimensionality. This phenomenon is exemplified by a nonlinear delay parabolic equation, which, through a linear transformation, maps to a corresponding linear delayed diffusion equation. Consequently, the solution to this latter equation can be expressed using a heat kernel featuring a maximum principle and exhibiting exponential decay. Furthermore, we prove that, for sufficiently large delay parameters, the original nonlinear equation admits a unique global-in-time solution that converges exponentially to its linear counterpart. The findings in this article are validated with the aid of simulations.

This study presents two distinct interpretations—denotational and operational—for higher-order probabilistic languages featuring first-class distributions. While our operational semantics offers a straightforward mapping to sampling algorithms, the denotational framework supports a rigorous exploration of program equivalence. To illustrate this equivalence, we analyze both pure and impure contexts, with the latter utilizing Felleisen's context lemma.

This paper introduces an innovative approach to design mining that enhances both conclusion stability and cross-project relevance. By leveraging knowledge graphs to represent design patterns, the approach enables the extraction of relevant information across different layers of a software architecture. Additionally, the study refines text-based conclusions through a combination of knowledge-aware and similarity-aware strategies. Empirical evaluations conducted on six datasets confirm that the proposed methodology significantly improves performance in these areas.

I have demonstrated that the future de Sitter horizon in holographic dark energy is mathematically equivalent to the total negative-pressure dark vacuum energy, which exists alongside a positive-pressure holographic dark matter component. By applying the generalized second law of thermodynamics to this framework, I derived the modified Friedmann acceleration equation, distinguishing it from the standard version by an extra term representing the active pressure of the holographic dark matter. When this equation of motion is applied, I found that the current cosmic acceleration is dominated by the vacuum energy's negative pressure, whereas cosmic deceleration in the past resulted from the positive pressure of the dark matter component.

Although functions are differentiable only on subsets defined by specific parameter configurations, recognizing these 'differentiability manifolds' is crucial for numerous applications. This paper demonstrates that knowledge of such manifolds can significantly enhance optimization performance. We propose an algorithm to identify differentiability manifolds by leveraging commutativity among gradient-based updates, a property that holds when continuous symmetries are embedded within the problem, or arises from specific structural characteristics. By partitioning the search domain into these manifolds, we can tailor optimization strategies to their unique geometry, thereby improving convergence rates. Our approach is validated through experiments on blind deconvolution tasks, where the search space is segmented into blind transfer function (BTF) manifolds. Optimization within these isolated BTF manifolds yields a restored camera function that is easier to recover, resulting in superior deconvolution outcomes.

An ideal $I$ within a commutative ring with unity is termed *weakly 1-absorbing* if it is proper and satisfies the condition that for any $1$-absorbing property regarding the product of three elements; specifically, whenever the product of three ring elements is proper and contained in $I$, then at least one of those elements or the quotient ideal (after removing a single element) must also be proper and contained in $I$. An *1-absorbing property* implies that this absorption occurs specifically upon removing an absorbing prime factor. While every weakly 1-absorbing property need not exclude non-proper ideals after removal, it is observed that the cube of any such ideal (excluding those already 1-absorbing) results in an ideal with these same characteristics. Furthermore, for any multiplicative subset $S$ disjoint from $I$, the localized ring exhibits a 1-absorbing property regarding the localized ideal if and only if the characteristic equation involving $|S|$ and the absorption properties holds true. Additionally, by examining the absorption of 2-element subsets, a 1-absorbing property is confirmed to be equivalent to requiring the absence of 2-element subsets whose product lands within $I$, provided the overall quotient ideal is not prime.

The observed correlation lag offers valuable insights for astrophysical observations. It enables the estimation of the time evolution of the source, serving as a basis for constructing interpolation or extrapolation schemes that anticipate future states or analyze past variations. However, the reliability of these schemes hinges on the accuracy of the correlation lag itself. This study examines how various fitting methods influence the confidence intervals surrounding the correlation lag and assesses the reliability of temporal prediction methods by simulating light curves. The results indicate that prediction methods yield robust confidence intervals when the correlation lag confidence interval is small, though prediction reliability diminishes as the uncertainty in the correlation lapdr increases.

Relational models in pharmacology, such as those depicting drug-target interactions or multi-target drugs, have been effectively addressed using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). However, current literature predominantly focuses on optimizing prediction accuracy for single tasks, often overlooking other critical performance dimensions necessary for deploying these systems in practical pharmacological scenarios. This study introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework for relational machine learning models in pharmacology, grounded in a composable set of metrics. We propose an innovative metric, Query-Level F1, to assess a model's capacity to retrieve pertinent neighbors within a graph. Additionally, we define Interaction F1 as a measure of a model's precision in identifying drug-target interactions. To benchmark these models, we constructed a specialized library of queries and constructed reference "gold standard" graphs representing known interactions; these libraries are accessible via an open-source repository. Applying our custom metrics to existing metrics reveals that current models struggle significantly with recalling drug-target associations. Consequently, our proposed composite metrics offer a nuanced assessment of a model's utility across diverse real-world pharmacological applications. The comprehensive code required to replicate this study is hosted publicly on GitHub.

This paper introduces an innovative method for road condition monitoring that leverages smartphones. The proposed system automatically captures images of the road surface, which are then analyzed to identify potholes. The core novelty of this approach is its country-agnostic framework, enabling the generation of road condition maps across diverse global locations. The methodology utilizes a machine learning classifier trained on smartphone camera data to detect potholes. The system's effectiveness is validated across three diverse countries, with the resulting maps demonstrating the approach's reliability in varying environments.

Imitation learning is a highly effective approach for acquiring new skills by observing expert demonstrations. A critical yet frequently overlooked issue is the discrepancy between the environment in which expert actions were recorded and the one in which the agent operates. Such a mismatch can lead to significant degradation in the resulting policy. To mitigate this, we introduce a novel strategy for the direct adaptation of demonstrated policies to the target environment by estimating and correcting for distributional shifts in state values. Our method remains model-free, requiring no prior knowledge of environmental dynamics. Experiments conducted within various simulated and real-world settings demonstrate that this technique substantially outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

The collapse of a rotating molecular cloud core initiates the formation of a protostar and an accretion disk. During this evolutionary phase, the disk may undergo gravitational fragmentation, potentially leading to the direct creation of binary or multiple star systems. The likelihood of this fragmentation is heavily influenced by the angular momentum the acceding material imparts to the disk. This study investigates the impact of varying angular momentum inputs on disk fragmentation by conducting simulations that trace the evolution of collapsing cores and their associated disks. The results indicate a clear trend: higher angular momentum leads to the formation of larger, thinner disks that are more susceptible to fragmentation. Specifically, fragmentation in highly rotating scenarios can commence earlier, within the initial accretion phase, rather than later in the disk's history. These findings offer valuable insights into the conditions under which direct disk fragmentation can occur during star formation.

Association rules serve as a fundamental method for uncovering relationships among items in extensive datasets. However, extracting every valid rule from such data is impractical due to their vast logical consistency; consequently, identifying and eliminating redundancies is crucial for enhancing interpretability. This study addresses characterizing and representing such redundancy through the lens of logical entailment. We propose a framework based on partial orders to define various forms of logical redundancy, analyze their interconnections, and characterize the measure of redundancy for individual rules as well as entire rule sets in terms of countable completeness. Furthermore, we characterize the problem of identifying irreducible set of rules free from specific types of redundancy and demonstrate that it generally constitutes an NP-complete challenge.

This study investigates crime recidivism by analyzing the impact of mental health interventions. Recidivism is classified as violent, property-related, or non-violent. The findings indicate that treatment significantly lowers the likelihood of violent and property crimes, though the effect on other crimes varies. The research utilizes a difference-in-differences method, comparing offenders with documented mental health conditions to those without, to establish a causal treatment effect. The analysis draws upon comprehensive data from the New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services, which tracks offender traits, criminal history, and mental health treatment records from 1991 to 2006. Results demonstrate that treatment reduces recidivism most effectively for violent and property offenses. The paper further explores the mechanisms behind these reductions, noting that treatment influences crime rates across various mental health diagnoses.

This paper establishes the recurrence relations, Stieljes moments, and generating functions for the polynomial sets resulting from the orthogonality with respect to the weight function $w(x)=\exp(-\int_{0}^{x}p(t)dt)$, where $p(t)$ denotes an arbitrary polynomial.

This paper introduces a novel approach for estimating radio maps in the millimeter-wave spectrum, where the system dynamically manages the uncertainty of the environment map to optimize the data gathering strategy for a specific task. The map uncertainty indicator is employed to formulate an optimization problem that determines the most effective measurement acquisition plan, the execution of which is achieved through an adaptive algorithm. The performance of the proposed framework is validated through a simulation study, demonstrating its potential for efficient and intelligent radio map estimation.

Anomaly detection is a critical research field with wide-ranging applications, including intrusion detection, fault diagnosis, and disease surveillance. While supervised methods rely on labeled data to train detectors, the scarcity of labeled anomalies renders this approach impractical for many real-world scenarios. Conversely, unsupervised techniques analyze the statistical properties of unlabeled normal data to identify deviations, making them ideal for contexts where labeling is unattainable. This work introduces a new deep learning framework for detecting anomalies in time-series data through unsupervised learning. The model employs an autoencoder to compress input data into a simplified representation and subsequently reconstructs it; anomalies are identified based on high reconstruction error, indicating a significant discrepancy from the learned patterns. Specifically, we develop a specialized series-representation autoencoder that isolates anomalies by modeling the series' core structure. By separating anomalies from normal data via this compression step, the system effectively identifies irregularities without requiring labeled examples.

This paper introduces a comparative analysis of verification systems utilizing static and dynamic techniques across three databases—Clean10, Clean100, and noisy variants of Clean100. Experiments were conducted under both clean and noisy acoustic conditions to evaluate the performance of these methods. While the outcomes demonstrate that the tested systems achieve comparable error rates in clean environments, the results in acoustic noisy conditions indicate that the dynamic approaches yield superior performance relative to their static counterparts.

Data augmentation is a well-established method for enhancing deep learning performance, particularly in computer vision, by synthesizing additional training samples through transformations like rotation, flipping, and color adjustments. This paper investigates how data augmentation impacts the utility of training data, specifically examining the relationship between original dataset size and the resulting performance improvements. By training ResNet-50 models on ImageNet using eight different augmentation strategies, the authors observed that larger datasets yield greater performance gains, indicating that augmentation effectively increases the utility of training data. Furthermore, the study introduces a novel metric, Data Quality Index (DQI), to quantify the value of individual images. The DQI demonstrates a strong positive correlation with both the effectiveness of specific augmentations and the magnitude of gains from data expansion, supporting a data-centric approach to deep learning.

This paper establishes conditions under which weak convergence of a sequence of statistical models enables weak convergence of corresponding M-estimator sequences, with applications to estimating structural breaks in the mean of a stochastic process. This approach permits the derivation of weak convergence for models that are not directly proven, by referencing a weaker convergent model through a perturbation argument, thereby estimating structural breaks in a significantly more straightforward manner.

This paper investigates how data dependency can exacerbate privacy risks in database management systems. We demonstrate that standard k-anonymity techniques fail to provide adequate protection when records are interlinked through dependencies. Consequently, we introduce a novel k-anonymity model incorporating dependency constraints, alongside efficient algorithms for the selective release of data while preserving both user privacy and dependency structures. Extensive experiments utilizing the LBG dataset confirm the effectiveness of our approaches.

This study investigates the effects of varying C/O ratios on the chemical evolution of protoplanetary disks, utilizing a 1D vertical model to simulate the physical and chemical dynamics of the midplane. We specifically examine the midplane environment of a 1 Myr-old disk, altering the C/O ratio between 0.1 and 1.0 while maintaining a fixed, uniform distribution of carbon and oxygen. Our findings indicate that increasing the C/O ratio results in a substantial rise in the column density of C$_2$H$_2$ and C$_2$H, particularly in the outer regions of the disk. Conversely, the abundances of H$_2$CO and CH$_3$OH remain largely unaffected by changes in the C/O ratio. We also observe that the C$_2$H$_2$/CO abundance ratio peaks at approximately 0.1 au for all modeled C/O ratios, a consequence of the high C/H abundance ratio facilitating the formation of HCCO, which subsequently reacts with H$_2$CO to produce H$_2$C$_3$O. Furthermore, the formation of CH$_3$OH is driven by the reaction of CH$_3$O with H, a process initiated by the reaction of O$_2$ with H to form OH, followed by subsequent reactions with CH$_3$. Our results suggest that the C$_2$H$_2$/CO ratio can serve as a diagnostic tool for determining the C/O ratio

Time-tagging systems are extensively employed in scientific research to record synchronized data from various sensors. These tags, representing precise event occurrence times, facilitate the calculation of inter-event delays and temporal correlations. However, the volume of such data is often excessive for manual inspection, necessitating the use of specialized software. This utility introduces the Extensible Time-tag Analyzer (ETA), a Python program capable of ingesting time-tagged datasets and performing comprehensive statistical analyses. Specifically, the ETA can process data from scientific setups involving up to 1000 synchronized photodiodes, resulting in up to 1000 million individual delay values. By utilizing vectorized operations within the NumPy library, the software accelerates statistical computations by several orders of magnitude compared to standard methods.

We investigate the connection between equilibria in mean field game (MFG) models and Nash equilibria within a Nash-Cournot framework adapted to inelastic strategic interactions. In this specific context, the condition of regularity presents a complication regarding equilibrium existence. We demonstrate that under the assumption of sufficiently high regularity, an MFG equilibrium can be constructed by utilizing the Nash equilibria of the corresponding Nash-Cournot game. Additionally, we present an illustrative example to confirm that, in the general case, an MFG equilibrium may persist even when the broader solution concept of a Nash equilibrium for the Nash-Cournot model is the only available solution.

We have conducted a chemical analysis of 10 new field stars belonging to the Ursa Major moving group (imprecisely referred to as the "Major String" in some contexts), utilizing high-resolution spectra from the MIKE spectrograph on the Magellan Baade Telescope. The study determined abundances for Fe-peak elements, alpha-elements, and light elements, comparing the results with previous data for 14 previously studied string members and a control group of 14 local stars. The new measurements were benchmarked against existing literature values for the original targets, yielding mean elemental abundances that align well with prior studies. The data indicate that the chemical composition of the string is more homogeneous than that of the local control group. Furthermore, the analysis reveals no evidence of pollution by heavy elements (s-, r-, or c-process) in either the string or the local group. The findings for the string are consistent with predictions from Galactic chemical evolution models, which posit an interstellar medium enriched by core-collapse supernovae and asymptotic giant branch stars, but not by neutron star mergers or rare events like supernovae Ia or Type I events.

User-generated content in fashion, particularly original outfit assemblies by users, is growing rapidly. Although such outfits often reflect the creator's unique style, stylistic preferences sometimes lead to inconsistencies, such as pairing mismatched garments. To address this, we present a new detection task aimed at identifying inappropriate or ill-fitting items within user-assembled fashion looks. We contend that effectively spotting these suboptimal items requires not only recognizing individual object attributes but also comprehending the visual and semantic compatibility between them. To this end, we propose FFMNet, a novel network that integrates fine-grained object analysis with comprehensive outfit-level compatibility assessment. Our method employs an attention-driven mechanism to pinpoint mismatched items, a capability validated by top-tier performance on the widely used ASIS dataset. Source code and model weights can be accessed at: https://github.com/ysj001/FFMNet.

The study of resource theories is pivotal in recent developments of quantum information. Within these theories, classical and quantum frameworks serve as foundational elements. By adopting a classical perspective, we can establish a broader, unified resource theory that encompasses various existing models. We introduce the concept of "resourceful probability distributions," which form the core of this ConAxiomatic approach. Specifically, we examine how these distributions can be transformed via operations defined by specific constraints (axioms), and we identify corresponding transformation-invariant quantities (data) that remain unchanged under those transformations. We demonstrate that this general structure effectively includes resource theories of entanglement, entropic uncertainty, and privacy within the quantum setting. Furthermore, we explore the connection between these constraints and the majorization relation, and we outline potential avenues for future investigation within these related concepts.

Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning framework designed to protect client privacy by transmitting only encrypted model updates rather than raw data. Nevertheless, standard FL algorithms often struggle with scalability as client numbers grow, and they face additional challenges when data is unevenly distributed across devices. To address these limitations, this paper introduces FedBuff, an innovative buffer-aided FL protocol that ensures privacy-driven scalability. The method operates by selectively buffering a small subset of clients per communication round to reduce the frequency of expensive global aggregation steps. Additionally, buffered clients perform multiple local training iterations, allowing them to better compensate for their limited representation within the active subset. The authors also derive the optimal buffer selection policy to ensure every client contributes sufficiently to learning. Experimental results demonstrate that FedBuff achieves superior performance compared to existing FL methods, particularly in environments with significant data heterogeneity.

We develop and analyze a unified operator calculus applicable to $n$-tuples consisting of $n \ge 1$ polynomial shift semigroups. For any $n$, this calculus is universal among those satisfying the commutation relations of the corresponding $n$-tuple of polynomial shift semigroups. When $n=2$, we demonstrate that their joint commutant consists precisely of the images generated by a newly defined two-variable calculus, which resolves—and thus disproves—the commutation relationsхай hypothesis raised in P. Surla's 2019 paper. For cases where $n \ge 3$, however, we provide counterexamples showing the existence operators that commute with the joint semigroup yet arise outside the defined multilinear calculus, thereby indicating that the commutant strictly exceeds what the calculus generates.

We propose a framework in which the entire universe is composed of dark matter and light matter, consisting of ordinary matter and a dominant component of cold, electroweak-scale Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs). This scenario is viable because the annihilation of primordial black holes (PBHs) can account for the observed abundance of WIMPs through their decay into fermion-antifion pairs. We find that PBHs with masses between $10^{-20}$ and $10^{-18}$ solar masses can account for the required WIMP density, a regime where these black holes are stable against Hawking evaporation. This mass scale is significant as it corresponds to the formation time of the first stars, implying a natural connection between WIMP production and the collapse of those primordial stars. Furthermore, we investigate the implications of this model for the formation of supermassive black holes.

This study examines the dynamics of a particle raft situated at the air-water interface, focusing on a system where particles interact via short-range repulsion. Utilizing a model that treats particles as hard disks, we demonstrate that the competition between particle re-aggregation and the surrounding fluid's expansion drives the periodic birth and expansion of rifts. Our findings indicate that the spacing between these adjacent rifts remains constant over time, a phenomenon explained by a balance between the temporal decay of raft elasticity and the increase in the elastic network's periodicity. Furthermore, we derive the mechanical properties of the gaseous state of the raft and the semi-elastic nature of the solid state.

Gallium nitride (GaN) is a highly valued nitride semiconductor capable of operating at extreme temperatures and high electric fields, making it suitable for demanding electronic applications. However, its intrinsic properties are hindered by a large lattice mismatch with conventional group-IV substrates, prompting efforts to develop lattice-matched GaN films on ternary compound semiconductor buffers. This study investigates the growth of such films on ZnGeN$_2$ and MgSiN$_2$ layers, which share nearly identical lattice parameters with GaN. Using first-principles density functional theory, we analyze the bond lengths and angles within these materials to determine their ideal growth orientations. Subsequently, we examine the band structures and effective masses of charge carriers to assess potential mobility enhancements. Our findings indicate that growing room-temperature grown, epitaxially matched GaZn on a ZnGeN$_2$ (01-10) buffer layer could achieve hole mobilities as high as 1000 cm$^2$/Vs at 300 K, a substantial increase from the standard GaN value of approximately 200 cm$^2$/Vs. Additionally, effective mass calculations for holes and electrons in both ZnGeN$_2$ and MgSiN$_2$ suggest promising potential for future high-speed, high-frequency device applications.

This paper introduces a semi-parametric policy gradient function approximation technique tailored for sample-based actor-critic algorithms in underwater navigation. By integrating a parametric value function within the sample-based actor-critic framework, we employ the SPGP actor-critic approach to enhance computational efficiency during function approximation and boost learning speed. Crucially, the inclusion of SPGP-SARSA for off-policy on-line policy evaluation allows for a substantial reduction in the number of samples required per update compared to traditional methods. We validate the efficacy of this algorithm through underwater robotic vehicle navigation simulations and compare its performance against standard Gaussian actor-critic, SPGP, and DDPG algorithms. Empirical results demonstrate that the SPGP-SARSA-driven function significantly accelers convergence, confirming the overall effectiveness of the proposed spactral method for underwater navigation applications.

We construct new isothermic surfaces from simply connected regions by applying Galilean transformations, rotations, inversions, and the GALILEAN TRANSFORMATIONS, including rotation and inversion. These surfaces are defined by a family of discrete Blaschke nets, which are generated by applying these transformations to a family of circles. We derive formulas for the first fundamental form of the resulting isothermic surfaces and demonstrate how their Minkowski lightlike congruences correspond to those of the original Blaschke nets.

This paper investigates the application of kernel methods to the stochastic Burgers equation, a fully nonlinear, fully coupled partial differential equation. We demonstrate that these kernel techniques offer a viable approach for approximating both parametric and functional components of the solution. Our findings indicate that, compared to traditional Galerkin projections which may suffer from a loss of convergence rates, direct kernel-based projections maintain the original spectral properties of the solution. Additionally, we establish the approximation capabilities of these methods in spaces of infinite dimensions and provide an analysis of their parametric dependencies. The proposed algorithm is validated through numerical experiments, illustrating its high efficiency and effectiveness.
This study introduces r-Krull-Dirichlet polynomials and Krull-r-analogues of Dowling polynomials, establishing connections to various established combinatorial frameworks.

While recent years have seen significant advancements in knowledge graph embedding techniques, few have specifically addressed time-aware instances. This paper introduces SEWE, a Stand-alone Time Embedding model for Knowledge Graphs. SEWE enhances temporal embeddings by integrating multiple time intervals, enabling efficient and effective time-aware link prediction. Our extensive experiments on two real-world benchmarks, including the Mini and full versions of the 24M dataset, demonstrate that SEWE outperforms state-of-the-art approaches like Temporal Knowledge Graph Embeddings. Additionally, we introduce a novel link scoring approach that rivals traditional methods. To further validate its efficacy, ablation studies and time sensitivity analyses were conducted, with results confirming SEWE's superior performance across various scenarios.

Let $X$ and $Y$ represent the strong shift equivalence (SSE) closures of $m$-fold and $n$-fold graph shifts derived from graphs $G$ and $H$, respectively. We demonstrate that $X$ and $Y$ are strongly shift equivalent if and only if $m=n$ and the graphs $G$ and $H$ possess corresponding insplits and outsplits such that their respective quotient graphs are strongly shift equivalent as single-fold shifts. Furthermore, we define an invariant taking values in the abelian monoid of isomorphism classes of graph shifts under the relation of strong shift equivalence. This concept generalizes the strong shift equivalence type invariant proposed by Boyle and Pavlov, which was restricted to graph shifts of multiplicity one.

We investigate the anisotropic character of the complex heavy-quark potential by incorporating new structural elements into its model. These features include an in-depth exploration of the potential's imaginary component, which represents the heavy-quark decay width, alongside terms of anisotropic and non-vanishing vacuum contraction types. Furthermore, we examine how these contributions influence the binding of the heavy-quark pair, the positions of corresponding heavy-quarkonia resonances, and the decay widths associated with their decays into light hadrons.

This paper introduces OREO-LM, a specialized language model designed to address questions requiring external knowledge. By integrating a Knowledge Interaction Layer (KIL) that enables direct access to external sources, the model surpasses closed-knowledge alternatives like QA-LM and standard QA models in F1 score by 10.1, 14.5, and 8.9 points respectively on the TQA, ScienceQA, and SQuAD datasets. Furthermore, we demonstrate targeted fine-tuning capabilities for specific subtasks, including multi-hop reasoning and natural language inference. Our analysis reveals that while the KIL significantly enhances performance, the model's behavior is heavily influenced by its learning dynamics and the probability distributions over external knowledge, ultimately suggesting that future progress in question answering depends on aligning external information with internal language representations.

High dimensional expanders are hypergraph structures generalizing expander graphs, holding promise for various applications in theoretical computer science. This survey introduces their foundational concepts and properties, reviews current research directions, and highlights potential benefits in areas such as high-dimensional topological quantum computation, the design of round-based communication protocols, and the derandomization of probabilistic algorithms.

Recent studies indicate that large language models (LLMs) possess the capacity to handle tasks outside their pre-training domain, yet the boundaries of this capability remain poorly understood. This study investigates the limits by examining performance on prompt variations not included during pre-training, revealing that LLMs can still handle completely unseen prompts effectively. Specifically, we find that prompts not previously encountered yield lower performance, yet remain within feasible operational ranges. Furthermore, we analyze how prompts shared features with known instances; even when novel, these similar prompts enhanced model outcomes. These findings suggest LLMs exhibit greater flexibility and robustness than previously recognized, supporting continued exploration into both the potentials and constraints of their capabilites.

This paper investigates the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{E})$ where $E$ is a $p$-adic field, focusing on $p$-ordinary representations. We present a generalization of Emerton's classification of such representations in the $p$-ordinary setting. Specifically, we demonstrate how Hida theory offers geometric guidance for selecting the appropriate $p$-ordinary (regular) submodules from the infinite family associated with each topologically finite-dimensional irreducible dual representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$; this selection is achieved via $p$-adic families constructed from modular forms. We also generalize these findings to the case of $p$-adic groups involving other $p$-adic fields.

Rydberg atoms are highly sensitive to external environments, making them ideal for various sensing and measurement applications. However, these experiments are often hindered by noise, which degrades measurement precision and limits performance. In this study, we apply deep learning to enhance the sensing capabilities of Rydberg atom-based systems despite such noise. Our approach utilizes a convolutional neural network to analyze Rydberg atom fluorescence images, allowing for the extraction of key information like Rydberg state occupancy and detuning even when noise is present. We validate our method through both simulations and laboratory experiments, demonstrating a significant improvement in signal-to-noise ratio compared to traditional linear analysis techniques. Notably, our model successfully learns the relationship between fluorescence imagery and detuning, enabling accurate linear extrapolation of detuning with a coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of 0.99 in the detuning range of -1 GHz to 1 GHz. Ultimately, this work illustrates that deep learning can effectively suppress the impact of noise within quantum sensing and measurement protocols involving Rydberg atoms, a strategy that holds promise for application across other quantum systems.

We have analyzed the H\(\text{II}\) region population of UGC 8839, a nearby (14.5 Mpc) edge-on spiral galaxy, utilizing emission lines from the HST/ACS G700M grism. The data were reduced and corrected for the effects of the galaxy's rotation, and the resulting spectra were modeled to derive the H\(\alpha\) surface brightness, H\(\beta\) surface brightness, and the equivalent width of H\(\alpha\). The H\(\alpha\) surface brightness was then compared with the surface brightness of the neutral hydrogen (HI) disk to calculate the HI-to-H\(\alpha\) ratio. Additionally, the equivalent width of H\(\alpha\) was used to estimate the star formation timescale, while the H\(\alpha\)-to-H\(\beta\) ratio served to quantify the extinction. The study reveals that the H\(\alpha\)-derived star formation surface density is approximately 1.5 times higher in the inner regions than in the outer regions of the HI disk, whereas the star formation timescale remains roughly constant across the galaxy. Furthermore, the HI-to-H\(\alpha\) ratio shows a slight increase with galactocentric radius, suggesting that H\(\alpha\)-emitting star-forming regions are more concentrated toward the center. The derived extinction values, ranging from 0.5 to 1.0 magnitudes, are consistent with previous

We approximate the Hausdorff dimension of the Julia set for a quasiregular endomorphism of the 3-sphere, $Q^3$, by utilizing a shift map defined on the space of infinite sequences formed by positive integers. This approximation holds even for self-maps $f$ of $Q^3$ that admit a rational representation as a Schreier graph arising from a covering of the real line.

The study utilizes data from the Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution (MAVEN) Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer (NGIMS) to examine gravity wave (GW) characteristics in the upper Martian atmosphere, specifically within the thermosphere and exosphere, by analyzing longitudinal and latitudinal variations in mass spectrometry ion composition data. These variations are used to derive wave amplitudes, which are then correlated with temperature and wind profiles to assess GW behavior. Results indicate that GW activity generally strengthens with increasing altitude up to approximately 200 km, after which it declines; this trend aligns with prior GW observations in the lower atmosphere. Additionally, GW activity exhibits a distinct minimum around 30° latitude, correlating with the presence of horizontal stratospheric jets. The findings also reveal a strong link between GW activity and temperature fluctuations: while temperature correlations are positive below 200 km, they reverse to negative at higher altitudes. These results provide critical insights into GW dynamics in the Martian upper atmosphere and their effects on thermospheric conditions.

Heavy vector mesons are predominantly produced in photovector events at the LHC, with the $J/\psi$ being the heaviest available. This paper employs vector-meson dominance to investigate the photoproduction of $Z/\psi$ within the framework of ultraperipheral heavy-ion collisions occurring at the LHC. We examine the $Z/\psi$ cross-sections across various impact parameters and analyze the dependencies on the $Z/\psi$ transverse momentum, comparing our findings with existing experimental data. Additionally, we explore how these quantities vary with the $Z/\psi$ rapidity and transverse momentum to assess how well our theoretical model aligns with the measurements.

This study introduces a novel SpectroGAN framework for audio generation, which integrates a spectrogram-based perceptual loss to emphasize perceptual spectrogram quality. Additionally, the model incorporates a reconstruction loss that minimizes the discrepancy between actual and predicted spectrograms by focusing on local spectral attributes. By harmonizing these complementary objectives, the proposed SpectroGAN effectively balances global spectral characteristics and precise values. For time-series input, this model generates high-fidelity melpectrograms and subsequently converts them into natural-sounding waveforms through a trained Griffin-Lim post-processing validator. Experimental results confirm that our proposed approach significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art autoencoders in both spectrogram prediction and audio reconstruction.

Fully connected Recurrent Neural Networks (FC-RNNs) are highly effective for sequential tasks but are susceptible to degradation caused by vanishing or exploding gradients during training. Although gradient clipping serves as a standard mitigation strategy, it often results in poor generalization performance. This study introduces a new approach to enhance FC-RNN training by directly constraining gradients to remain within a specified norm threshold, thereby improving generalization. The proposed method is grounded in the observation that effective FC-RNN learning requires gradients to exhibit both low variance and a small magnitude. By directly controlling gradient size and variance, the technique accelerates learning and boosts overall generalization capabilities. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark datasets for tasks including character-level language modeling and speech recognition demonstrate that this approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

The rapid spread of the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) has necessitated the implementation of containment strategies to mitigate the disparity between medical effectiveness and economic impact. This study introduces a new approach for designing these measures using a data-driven, physics-informed mathematical model capable of being solved with only minimal parameters. By applying a multi-objective optimization framework, the method generates a range of policy options, allowing the selection of specific, timely interventions that best balance public health and economic considerations. The proposed optimization algorithm is both computationally efficient and easy to use, enabling the quick adaptation to new data. The results indicate that a multi-phase moderate restriction policy offers an optimal equilibrium between saving lives and preserving the economy. The efficacy of this model was validated using real-world data from the Italian region of Lombardy.

This paper presents DataScope, an interactive environment designed to streamline the visualization and analysis of machine learning (ML) data. Recognizing that ML pipelines often involve complex, multi-step transformations of real-world data, traditional debugging methods struggle to effectively isolate and rectify issues. To address this, DataScope employs a Data Dependency Graph (DDG) to represent relationships across various data stages, facilitating the identification of anomalies through user interaction. Users can navigate these stages to inspect data characteristics, annotate problematic instances, and rectify errors within the DDG interface. Evaluation results from both controlled studies and real-world ML applications demonstrate that DataScope significantly accelerates data debugging compared to conventional approaches. The system is accessible at https://datascopedx.github.io/.
